## Cases

### Video streaming that had to outlive its hardware

- Cisco, 2010–2014
- Limit: 64 MB RAM · 6-year hardware lifecycle
- Problem: Real-time video on 64 MB of RAM, on hardware expected to ship for six years.
- Decision: Design every software choice to survive years without a hardware redesign.
- Result: Shipped and held for the product's lifecycle.
- 64 MB RAM budget (source: résumé)
- 6 yr hardware lifecycle (source: résumé)
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### Carrier platform parts that partners could extend

- Mavenir, 2014–2018
- Limit: Carrier-grade production
- Problem: Carrier networks needed IMS, RCS and SIP components that other teams and partners could build on.
- Decision: Put extensibility patterns in early, even when shipping a single feature would have been faster.
- Result: Extensibility patterns used by partner integrations.
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### Millions of sessions, zero tolerance for failure

- Mavenir · Rakuten Link, 2018–2021
- Limit: Zero tolerance for failure
- Problem: Programs shipped without acceptance criteria; problems surfaced in customer validation, the most expensive place to find them.
- Decision: Define SLOs and invest in telemetry before features; manage performance against cost and operability.
- Result: 99.99% uptime; integration failures down 20%; 30% engineering capacity freed.
- 99.99% uptime (source: résumé)
- −20% integration failures (source: résumé)
- +30% engineering capacity freed (source: résumé)
- −20% support tickets (source: site)
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### From shipping by calendar to shipping by readiness

- Mavenir · T-Mobile Digits, 2019–2024
- Limit: SLA penalties trending to $2M/quarter
- Problem: SLA penalties were trending toward $2M a quarter on a 1M-user, API-first platform whose release calendar was the strategy.
- Decision: Rebalance investment from 90/10 to 50/50 feature-to-stability, and ship by readiness signals instead of dates.
- Result: Stability targets met in six months; the quality record won Rakuten as a customer. Time-to-market 12 → 9 weeks.
- 1M+ users on the platform (source: résumé)
- −25% release cycle, 12→9 weeks (source: résumé)
- $2M+ SLA exposure avoided (source: résumé)
- −15% downtime (source: site)
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### Simpler API contracts, 30% more revenue

- Mavenir · T-Mobile Digits, 2019–2024
- Limit: Zero added ops load
- Problem: Enterprise and SMB segments were underserved; partner integrations needed hand-holding.
- Decision: Simplify the API contracts and make partner integration self-serve, instead of customising per partner.
- Result: About 30% incremental revenue with zero added operational load.
- +30% incremental revenue (source: résumé)
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### Data-sharing contracts with Samsung, Apple and Amazon

- Mavenir · T-Mobile Digits, 2019–2024
- Problem: The platform needed API data-sharing agreements across 40+ device types.
- Decision: Negotiate the contracts directly; present the trade-offs to the C-suite in QBRs.
- Result: Agreements across 40+ device types.
- 40+ device types (source: résumé)
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### Principal Engineer to product manager, deliberately

- UBC Sauder, 2024–2026
- Problem: Engineering depth without the commercial language to argue for it.
- Decision: Leave a principal-engineer track; do an MBA in tech and analytics.
- Result: MBA, UBC Sauder (Tech & Analytics).
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### 0-to-1 decision support in a domain he'd never worked in

- Vancouver Airport Authority, 2025–2026
- Limit: No new headcount, systems or budget
- Problem: Operators ran multi-million-dollar asset allocation at peak on gut instinct. The data existed; no decision layer did.
- Decision: Go airside before writing a spec; define KPIs before the first sprint; ship with no new headcount, systems or budget.
- Result: Idle time cut 50% (20% → 10%); about $500K downtime prevented; delivered in 7 months.
- −50% fleet idle time (source: résumé)
- $500K downtime prevented (source: résumé)
- 15+ operators interviewed (source: résumé)
- 99% continuity at peak (source: site)
- [Résumé](https://kachajugaad.github.io/Ashutosh_Shukla_Resume.pdf)

### Radios that read the weather forecast

- Independent · TelcoEdge, 2026
- Limit: Sovereign data only
- Problem: Rural 5G drops calls in bad weather because towers react after the signal fails.
- Decision: Pre-adjust radio settings from Government of Canada forecasts; sovereign data only, no API keys or US endpoints.
- Result: Error rate 13.02% → 12.33% on the prairie (a 5.3% relative drop, simulated); 332 tests passing.
- 5.3% fewer errors, prairie (simulated) (source: public)
- 332 tests passing (source: public)
- 0.0% Arctic result, published (source: public)
- [Live dashboard](https://kachajugaad.github.io/TelcoEdge/)
- [Essay](https://ashutoshukla.substack.com/p/your-cell-signal-drops-every-time)

### Will my next call drop? A map that knows the weather

- Independent · TelcoEdge, 2026
- Limit: Zero carrier dependencies
- Problem: Canadians have no carrier-independent way to know if a call will drop.
- Decision: Fuse public tower and weather data; no carrier agreement needed.
- Result: Every Canadian postal code; six weather scenarios.
- 32,756 tower sites indexed (source: public)
- 6 weather scenarios (source: public)
- [Live tool](https://kachajugaad.github.io/TelcoEdge/signal-forecast/)

### Edge AI that degrades gracefully, offline

- Independent · AEdge, 2026
- Limit: Offline, deterministic latency
- Problem: Fleet vehicles fail expensively; drivers find out after the damage.
- Decision: Three-tier inference (deep learning → statistical ML → expert rules) with a designed fallback, instead of one fragile model.
- Result: <100 ms signal-to-alert (p99); 145 tests; 2nd place, ProductBC Build-a-thon 2026.
- <100 ms signal to alert, p99 (source: public)
- 145 tests passing (source: public)
- 2nd ProductBC Build-a-thon 2026 (source: public)
- [Live site](https://kachajugaad.github.io/AEdge/)
- [ProductBC](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/productbc_thats-a-wrap-to-our-6-week-productbc-build-a-thon-activity-7444590918839640065-xPJ6)

### Carrier APIs without a procurement agreement

- Independent · camara-dev, 2026
- Limit: Procurement wall
- Problem: Canadian developers couldn't test carrier APIs without signing a procurement agreement.
- Decision: Remove the obstacle instead of adding a feature: an open sandbox with carrier simulation profiles.
- Result: First API call in 90 seconds; 53 tests.
- 90 s to first API call (source: public)
- 53 tests passing (source: public)
- [GitHub](https://github.com/KachaJugaad/camara-dev)
- [Essay](https://ashutoshukla.substack.com/p/the-network-already-knows-nobody)

### Is this real? Honest confidence, not false certainty

- Independent · realEngine, 2026
- Limit: Privacy: 60-second deletion
- Problem: People can't tell whether media is AI-generated.
- Decision: Show probability-based confidence instead of a yes/no verdict; delete files within 60 seconds.
- Result: Verdict in under 8 seconds on two platforms.
- <8 s detection verdict (source: public)
- 2 platforms (source: public)
- [Live site](https://realengine.ca)

### Reading the AI-fabric specs, and writing down the gap

- Independent · Building AI Factory, 2026
- Limit: Only claims a spec page supports
- Problem: AI factories run on new network standards most product people never read.
- Decision: Read UE 1.1, OCP NIC Core and ESUN line by line; claim only what a page supports.
- Result: 2 interactive figures, 1 brief, 1 fact check, 1 A4 poster.
- 2 live models (source: public)
- 21 statements fact-checked (source: public)
- [Fig 2 · UET spraying](https://kachajugaad.github.io/lab/uet-spray/)
- [Fig 1 · GPUDirect](https://kachajugaad.github.io/lab/gpudirect-rdma/)
- [Brief](https://kachajugaad.github.io/briefs/ue-nic-profile/)
- [Fact check](https://kachajugaad.github.io/briefs/ue-nic-profile/factcheck.html)

## Hard calls

- Sales wanted features. Engineering thought stability work was process. Call: Moved investment from 90/10 to 50/50 feature-to-stability. Cost: Six months of fewer features, argued to both camps.
- A new domain, peak-season pressure, and no budget for new staff or systems. Call: Went airside with ground crews before writing a single spec. Cost: Time spent listening before building.
- The Arctic test showed no improvement. Call: Published 0.0% next to the 5.3% prairie result. Cost: A weaker-looking headline.
- Partners wanted custom deals; operations could not take more load. Call: Simplified the API contracts and made integration self-serve. Cost: Saying no to bespoke partner requests.
- Developers were blocked by procurement, not by technology. Call: Built a sandbox instead of another feature. Cost: Building something no carrier asked for.
- A principal-engineer track with a clear path up. Call: Moved into product and did an MBA. Cost: Restarting mid-career.
